title: H8 – Employer branding
source: Zusammenfassung von Session 8 „Employer branding“ (Sparrow & Otaye, 2015; Mortensen & Edmondson, 2023; Randstad 2026)

blocks.text: Labour-market competition for key talent is increasing, so firms need an employer brand: the attributes that make them distinctive and the employer of choice for a desired target group.
Business case (Sparrow & Otaye, 2015): the brand manages the psychological contract, signals values and prestige, and creates a common identity for employees.
The employer brand is the overlap of identity (who I am) and image (what others see); it must be aligned with the corporate and product brand.
Build it in six steps: who am I · customers · competitors · distinctive EVP · create & communicate · evaluate impact.
A holistic EVP (Mortensen & Edmondson, 2023) offers material offerings, growth & development, connection & community, meaning & purpose.
Strong brands are insightful, clear, distinctive and consistent – the most common failure is a gap between external promise and internal experience.
Diagnose the gap: what does the campaign promise (image), what do employees and leavers report (identity)?
Check the target group: does the EVP fit the people the firm wants (young, diverse, mid-career women…)? Use Randstad/survey data and competitor mapping.
Fix the experience first (careers, leadership, flexibility), then communicate it – more advertising cannot fix an identity problem.
Link to recruitment: narrow channels (elite universities, referrals) limit diversity; signals in the brand attract people like the current workforce.
Measure impact: applications, offer acceptance, new-hire retention, engagement, external recognition.
The set of attributes and qualities that make an organisation distinctive and the employer of choice for a target group.
The set of attributes that the labour market and employees perceive as the value they gain through employment in the organisation.
The employee's beliefs about the mutual obligations of the employment deal – shaped already by recruitment messages.
Lombard Odier: what does Louise's resignation signal beyond the individual case – and is the EVP coherent for mid-career women?
